title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Prepaid Hours Standing Against the Hours of a Call
content:
**Term A.** Where the tier lets unused prepaid hours roll into the next program year and blocks bought
within the tier's expiry period stand on the program, the prepaid hours available to the call are the
hours of every block bought within that period less the hours drawn by the calls completed in the same
period ahead of it, and only the hours of the call beyond that balance are billed.

**Term B.** Where the tier lets no unused hours roll over but blocks stand bought since the current term
started, the prepaid hours available are the hours bought since the term start date less the hours drawn
since that day, and only the hours beyond that balance are billed.

**Term C.** In any other case no prepaid hours stand against the hours of the call.

**Term D.** The two figures of the Demand Service Rate Programs that Terms A and B turn on are the rollover term and the expiry period:

| Program | Unused hours roll into the next program year | Expiry period (calendar months) |
|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | No | 0 |
| Priority Response Program | No | 0 |
| Block Hour Service Program | Yes | 12 |
| Emergency Response Program | Yes | 12 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | Yes | 18 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | Yes | 24 |

**Term E — the terms in combination.**

| The program's rollover term | What stands on the program | The hours of the call that are billed |
|---|---|---|
| unused hours roll over | blocks bought within the expiry period | those beyond the hours of those blocks less the hours drawn by the calls completed in the same period ahead of this one |
| unused hours roll over | no block bought within the expiry period | all of them |
| unused hours do not roll over | blocks bought since the term start date | those beyond the hours bought since that date less the hours drawn since that date |
| unused hours do not roll over | no block bought since the term start date | all of them |

**Term F — an illustration.** On the Block Hour Service Program, where unused hours roll over and the
expiry period is 12 calendar months, blocks totalling 40 hours bought inside those 12 months against
which earlier calls completed in the same period have drawn 34 hours leave 6 prepaid hours available; a
call charged for 8 hours therefore has 2 hours billed. Where those earlier calls had drawn all 40 hours,
none would be available and all 8 hours would be billed.
